newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end 1.8 pct lower, but brokers unfazed.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end 1.8 pct lower, but brokers unfazed.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed 1.84 percent lower on Thursday on jitters induced by Wall Street's 100-point plunge on New Year's Eve.

"I wouldn't read too much into this," said Julian Ings Chambers in institutional sales at BZW Securities. "We will get a more sensible view on the market toward the end of next week when new money is readied for allocation."
The Hang Seng Index slumped 248.01 points to 13,203.44, inching up from the day's low of 13,200.23 at the close of trading.
Turnover was also a heavy HK$10.09 billion, nearly double Tuesday's half day session of HK$5.46 billion. The market was closed on Wednesday for the New Year holiday.

On Tuesday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 101.10 points or 1.54 percent to 6,458.27 on U.S. economic data showing a more robust economic performance, which rekindled fears of inflation and interest rate hikes.
Hang Seng Index futures took Wall Street's dive to heart. The January contract shed 330 points to 13,130 and February, which saw very little trade, was down 260 points to 13,250.
Brokers said they saw the Hong Kong market trending more in line with the Chinese business cycle.
"As more China operations are injected into Hong Kong red chips, growth is coming from well beyond Hong Kong," said Amy Wong, research director at New China Hong Kong.
But Wong said she expect further some consolidation following the strong run-up to the year-end.

The H share sector continued its strong run, with the Hang Seng China Enterprise Index closing up 5.92 percent at 1,038.60. Guangdong Kelong led the sector with a leap of HK$0.60 to HK$5.60 share. Shandong Xinhua advanced HK$0.35 to HK$2.65.
Red chips were also favoured. China Resources bounded ahead HK$0.80 to HK$18.20 on robust volume of HK$188.09 million.
The commercial and industrial sector was led the market down. Hutchison Whampoa retreated HK$2.00 down at HK$58.75. Wharf and Swire Pacific both declined HK$1.00 to HK$37.60 and HK$72.75.

In the property sector, New World Development held steady at HK$52.25 following the reports that the group would sell its 54.4 percent held Renaissance Hotel unit to Doubletree Corp in a deal worth US$850 million.
